data.description:
## Context / Problem

Change 3407 (merged as 9beecb409ab, bug unmedical-stational-chrysalis) made the MCP in-flight gauge call `release_freed_heap()` when its count returns to zero. `_malloc_trim()` (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:68`) resolves glibc's `malloc_trim` with `ctypes.CDLL(None)` and catches only `AttributeError` and `OSError`. On Windows, `ctypes.CDLL(None)` raises `TypeError: LoadLibrary() argument 1 must be str, not None`, so every release that takes the gauge to zero raises. That breaks every certified/signing tool call (`transition_ticket`, `verify_completion`, `review_plan`, `sign_manifest`, `sign_review`) and every direct gauge release on Windows.

## Observation

- GitHub Actions run 44002909290, job 133771119760 ("sweep (windows)", main at 390f926c7ea): 46 failures, all in MCP tests; the log contains 109 lines with `LoadLibrary() argument 1 must be str, not None`.
- Reproduced on macOS by patching `ctypes.CDLL` so `CDLL(None)` raises that `TypeError`: running the 16 affected test files on origin/main 57d45053272 gives 47 failures, a superset of all 46 Windows failures (including the parity `REJECTED`-vs-`ACCEPTED` cases and the missing `signed_at` case, which receive the `TypeError` as a failed tool call). The one extra, `test_close_picked_up_but_not_started_when_the_server_stops_never_runs`, does not run in the Windows sweep.

## Approach

Make `_malloc_trim()` return `None` on any platform that is not Linux, before touching `ctypes` (`sys.platform.startswith("linux")`), and keep the existing `AttributeError`/`OSError` catch for Linux C libraries without `malloc_trim` (musl). glibc is a Linux C library, so no other platform can have `malloc_trim`. No config key, environment variable, flag or other mechanism.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`: platform check in `_malloc_trim()`; docstring states the Windows case.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py`: Windows-shaped test.

## Testing

- New test: with `sys.platform` set to `win32`, `ctypes.CDLL(None)` patched to raise `TypeError` as on Windows, and the `_malloc_trim` cache cleared, `release_freed_heap()` returns `False` and a gauge `hold()` release does not raise. It fails on current main (the `TypeError` escapes) and passes with the fix.
- Re-run the 16 affected files under the same `ctypes.CDLL(None)` simulation: 0 failures expected.
- Existing Linux tests keep passing (`release_freed_heap()` is `True` on Linux; the idle-memory test still releases memory).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_malloc_trim()` returns `None` without calling `ctypes.CDLL` on non-Linux platforms, and `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py` passes.
- [ ] The new Windows-shaped test fails on origin/main 57d45053272 and passes with the fix.
- [ ] Under the `ctypes.CDLL(None)`-raises-`TypeError` simulation, the 16 test files that failed in job 133771119760 report 0 failures.
- [ ] `make verify` passes, and `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.
- [ ] After merge, a dispatched `test.yml` run on main has its "sweep (windows)" job pass; the run and job IDs are recorded here.
data.title: MCP certified and signing tools fail on Windows: the idle heap trim calls ctypes.CDLL(None), which raises TypeError there
